mark 2 · 15% less time 310°F / 155°C Gas mark 2 · 10% less time What recipes use 180°C 180°C (356°F, gas mark 4) is the default for cakes, quick breads, brownies, cookies, roast chicken, fish fillets, and tray bakes. It is the temperature recipes fall back to when the writer is not sure, so plenty of dishes sit here. A general recipe converts to 165°C in a basket air fryer. Baked goods take a smaller cut (dense batters need the heat to reach the centre); chicken and fish take the standard cut. The failure mode at 180°C: domed cake, raw middle The fan blows straight onto the top of a cake or bread, which browns and crusts while the middle is still liquid. The result is a cracked, domed top over a gummy centre. Three things fix it: use a shallower tin than the recipe calls for, tent the top loosely with foil for the first half of the cook (tuck the edges under so the fan cannot lift it), and test the middle with a skewer at the check time instead of trusting the colour. Paper liners must be weighed down by the batter; a loose sheet will lift into the element. Worked example (conventional) A Victoria sponge recipe says 180°C for 25 minutes. Cakes take a smaller cut, so a basket air fryer runs it at 170°C (335°F) for 21 minutes; test with a skewer at 15 minutes. An oven-style unit takes 170°C (340°F) for 23 minutes. Use a 15–18 cm tin on the crisper plate, filled halfway. Worked example (fan) If the recipe gives 160°C fan, the same cake converts to 150°C (305°F) in a basket air fryer for 24 minutes, checked at 17 minutes. An oven-style unit runs 155°C (310°F) for 25 minutes. Conventional vs fan at 180°C UK/EU recipes print "180°C / 160°C fan / gas mark 4". The conventional figure goes through the flagship engine (20–25°F cut), the fan figure through the convection engine (0–15°F cut). The gap between the two air fryer results is the fan offset: a fan-oven recipe is already part-way there, so the remaining cut is smaller. The converter widget on this page lets you switch. For frozen food packs, use the frozen mode — it keeps the temperature and cuts 30% time. For a general recipe, 165°C (330°F) in a basket air fryer with about 20% less time, or 170°C in an oven-style unit. Cakes and casseroles take a smaller cut; see the table. My recipe says 160°C fan — is that the same as 180°C conventional? Yes, that is the UK convention: fan = conventional − 20°C. Use the fan input on this page for a fan-oven recipe; it takes a gentler cut. What gas mark is 180°C? gas mark 4. The UK dial marks 180°C as gas mark 4. Can I use this for a frozen food pack that says 180°C? No — frozen packs follow different rules (keep the temperature, cut 30% time). Use the frozen mode instead. Why does the fan column give a different answer? A fan-oven recipe is already 20°C lower. The convection engine applies a smaller remaining cut (0–15°F, 5–10% time) because the fan has already done part of the work.
